neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were strangers. The incident occurred when the accused approached the victim and others to teach a lesson after a previous fight. The victim sustained multiple injuries to his head, including incised wounds and bone-deep cuts. The accused were armed with weapons such as a lathi, kulhari, and pharsa. The victim died as a result of the injuries. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence to establish the incident. However, the credibility of the eyewitnesses was questioned due to contradictions in their statements and the presence of previous enmity between the parties. The recovery of weapons from the accused was not fully established, and the statements of the witnesses were found to be inconsistent and unreliable.

legal_principle_applied.value: For trial under Section 302 IPC, if a witness is branded as untrustworthy having allegedly twisted the facts and made contrary statements, it is not safe to impose conviction on the basis of such witness's statement. When there is an effort to falsely implicate one accused person, the statement of such an eyewitness cannot be relied upon without strong corroboration.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the conviction of Mohd. Jamil (A2) under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC was set aside due to unreliable witness statements, but his conviction under Section 323 read with Section 34 IPC was maintained.
